## 非農優於預期，市場重新押注 Fed 升息

美國就業報告優於預期，週五美債殖利率大幅上升，不僅回吐週四的溫和漲勢，也使市場完全反映 Fed 在 12 月前升息的預期。5 月非農就業增加 17.2 萬人，高於所有預測，前兩個月的數據也獲上修。2 年期殖利率跳升 12 個基點至 4.17%，10 年期上升 8 個基點至 4.55%。

油價雖然繼續回落，仍未能支撐美債。10 年期名目殖利率的升幅全數來自實質殖利率，後者升至 2.19%，損益兩平通膨率則維持 2.36%。強勁的就業改變了市場對政策的判斷，也提高投資人要求的實質報酬。此前漲勢快速的科技股承受更大壓力，半導體指數重挫 10.26%，美元走強，黃金下跌。

融資市場並未隨之關閉。與 Google 有關的市政債發行後，次級市場利差收窄；Apollo 與 Blackstone 也完成總額 $350 億、用於 Anthropic 租用晶片的債務融資，但有無擔保的不同層級，融資成本差距明顯。美國以外，加拿大就業、日本薪資與印度上修的通膨預測，也使央行更難放鬆政策。接下來的通膨數據，將檢驗週五升溫的升息預期能否維持。

## 就業回升，前端殖利率領漲

週四初領失業金數據帶來的降溫印象，很快被 5 月就業報告扭轉。失業率維持 4.3%，勞動參與率為 61.8%；休閒與旅宿業新增 7 萬個職位，為逾三年來最多。數據公布後，美債立即下跌，2 年期殖利率盤中升幅創一年多來最大。

利率交換市場完全反映 Fed 在 12 月前升息 25 個基點，10 月升息機率約為 60%，6 月則仍預期維持利率不變。新任主席即將主持首次會議之際，克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁 Beth Hammack 表示，就業接近平衡，近期升息可能是合適的選擇。經濟學家的看法仍有落差：花旗預期就業將轉弱，維持年底前降息三次、每次 25 個基點的預測；高盛取消 12 月降息預測，但仍認為升息的可能性不高。

賣壓集中在殖利率曲線的前半段。5 年期殖利率上升 11 個基點至 4.29%，30 年期上升 4 個基點至 5.01%。2s10s 縮窄 4 個基點至 38 個基點，2s30s 縮窄 8 個基點至 84 個基點。全週來看，2 年、5 年、10 年與 30 年期分別上升 19、16、10 與 2 個基點。2s5s10s 蝶式利差上升 2 個基點至 −14 個基點，5 年期相對兩翼仍偏貴；2s10s30s 維持 −8 個基點。

實質殖利率也呈現前端升幅較大的走勢。5 年期上升 11 個基點至 1.81%，7 年期上升 9 個基點至 1.99%，10 年期上升 8 個基點至 2.19%；20 年與 30 年期則分別上升 5 與 3 個基點，來到 2.55% 與 2.74%。10 年期損益兩平通膨率當日持平，且低於一週及一個月前，顯示這次賣壓主要來自實質利率上升，而非長期通膨補償再度擴大。

稍晚公布的消費信貸顯示，家庭借款仍在增加。4 月消費信貸增加 $207.3 億，高於市場預估的 $178 億，3 月則修正為增加 $222.3 億。以年率計，信貸成長 4.8%，其中循環信用成長 10.4%，非循環信用成長 2.9%。這份數據在美東時間 15:00 公布，晚於上午的主要利率調整。信用卡借款加快，可能是支出仍強，也可能反映財務壓力，對家庭財務狀況的解讀並不如就業人數那麼明確。

最短端國庫券變化不大。4、6 與 8 週券的債券等值殖利率分別維持 3.68%、3.68% 與 3.69%，13 週券維持 3.71%；17、26 與 52 週券則依序上升 2、3 與 5 個基點，較長天期開始反映未來升息。選擇權市場也出現買進 7 月到期 10 年期美債買權的需求，押注殖利率回落至約 4.4%，涵蓋通膨公布與 Fed 會議期間，以因應數據較弱或政策指引不如預期鷹派的可能。

## 科技股重挫，融資市場仍有買盤

實質殖利率上升碰上此前快速累積的漲幅，科技股跌勢格外沉重。Nasdaq 100 下跌 4.77%，半導體指數下跌 10.26%，S&P 500 則下跌 2.64%；VIX 大漲 39.68% 至 21.51。除了利率，獲利了結、Broadcom 展望不如預期、Meta 可能透過股權籌資、比特幣走弱，以及投資人為大型發行案預留現金，都加重賣壓。資金轉向防禦產業，S&P 500 仍有五個類股收漲。

美元指數上升 0.66% 至 100.07，黃金期貨下跌 3.10% 至 $4,337.10。油價則回落，WTI 下跌 2.69% 至 $90.54，布蘭特下跌 2.04% 至 $93.09，不過兩者全週仍上漲。信用債 ETF 同樣收跌：LQD 下跌 0.62%、HYG 下跌 0.50%、JNK 下跌 0.44%，EMB 下跌 0.73%。

大型科技公司相關的融資，在初級市場仍能找到買家。California Community Choice Financing Authority 為 Pioneer Community Energy 發行約 $10 億預付能源市政債，由 Alphabet 擔任金融中介、高盛承銷，最大一批債券以高於基準 95 個基點定價。至週五下午，2035 年到期券成交額達 $4.92 億，平均利差 89 個基點，部分交易低至 74 個基點。這筆安排讓公用事業鎖定長期電力成本節省，也藉由新的交易對手吸引預付能源債買盤。

Apollo 與 Blackstone 完成的 $350 億晶片融資規模更大，投資人的風險也分成不同層級。Anthropic 將透過特殊目的公司租用 Google 設計的晶片，約半數債務已完成分銷。其中 $60 億優先級債務以高於美債 1 個百分點定價，另外 $240 億優先票據按面額發行，票息 5.75%。兩者均獲非公開的中段投資等級評等，並有 Broadcom 支持。

沒有 Broadcom 支持的 $45 億 B 級債務，同樣按面額發行，票息則達 8.5%。若租約違約後出售晶片，所得仍不足償還優先級投資人，Broadcom 同意補足差額。這項保障有助吸引保險公司與銀行參與優先級融資，次順位債務則承擔較多租金收入與晶片轉售價值風險。

個別交易順利完成，並未消除對整體借款規模的疑慮。DoubleLine 與 Oaktree 在週末的評論中，著重技術淘汰、資料中心同時大量興建，以及最終贏家尚不明朗的風險。大型雲端業者已在全球發行逾 $1,550 億無擔保債，較前一整年的發行額高出逾 45%；Bloomberg Intelligence 估計，未來五年 AI 資本支出約 $5 兆，其中相當部分仰賴債務融資。這些機構偏好能承受景氣循環的資產負債表與較佳回收保障，並未斷言目前債券估值已形成泡沫。

美國收盤後，川普表示仍考慮出售房利美與房地美股份，但並不急迫。先前方案包括以約 $5,000 億或更高估值出售 5%–15% 股份，可能籌得約 $300 億；隨著市場對執行的疑慮增加，兩家公司股價年內已下跌逾 30%。資本結構、政府支持及退出接管的條件，仍會影響機構融資與房貸利率，部分分析師警告出售股份可能推高借款成本。

其他企業的融資則涉及更困難的資產負債表調整。Raizen 收盤後公布庭外協議，涵蓋約 650 億雷亞爾、折合 $126 億債務，獲持有計畫內 75.5% 債權的債權人支持；其中 45% 將轉為股權，其餘 55% 交換為新債。日本週末公布的統計顯示，有申報數據的日經 225 成分企業，截至 3 月會計年度債務達 ¥678 兆，年增 4.6%，併購、投資與股東回饋持續消耗現金。日本製鐵因以 $140 億收購美國鋼鐵，借款約增為兩倍，並成為 S&P 降評的原因之一。國內利率上升將增加再融資成本，體質較弱的工業企業尤其承壓；若放款增速快於存款，部分融資也可能轉向債市。

## 就業與薪資回升，全球央行更難轉鬆

加拿大同樣出現超乎預期的就業增長。5 月新增就業 87,800 人，為 2024 年 12 月以來最多，遠高於預估的 1 萬人；失業率由 6.9% 降至 6.6%。全職招聘與多數產業同步改善，使 2 年期殖利率上升約 10 個基點至 2.911%，盤中升幅為 5 月 4 日以來最大，交換市場反映年底前升息逾 30 個基點。

不過，這次反彈尚未完全補回先前的疲弱。就業人數仍比 2025 年底少近 2.5 萬人，永久全職職位的薪資年增率則由 4.8% 降至 3.2%，低於預期的 4.6%。市場預期加拿大央行維持利率在 2.25%，後續指引需同時衡量就業明顯回升、薪資降溫與先前流失的職位。

日本薪資數據強化市場對日銀在 6 月 15–16 日會議升息 25 個基點的預期。實質薪資年增 1.9%，高於預估的 1.7% 與修正後前值 1.4%，連續第四個月增加；名目薪資增加 3.5%，基本薪資增加 3.4%，日銀關注的全職工作者薪資指標增加 2.6%。中東風險持續之下，薪資改善能否延續，仍取決於企業獲利與通膨。

印度央行一致決議維持附買回利率 5.25% 與中性立場，但將本會計年度通膨預測由 4.6% 上修至 5.1%。常備存款便利利率維持 5.00%，邊際常備便利利率與 Bank Rate 均為 5.50%。政策利率雖未調整，上修的物價預測已壓縮近期寬鬆空間。

台灣也面臨更高的進口成本壓力。5 月消費者物價年增率由 1.74% 升至 2.20%，儘管月增幅縮小；生產者物價年增率由 8.54% 升至 14.11%，美元計價進口物價則年增 17.21%。生產者物價月增幅放緩，尚不足以抵消進口投入成本與匯率換算帶來的壓力。

歐洲的通膨與成長矛盾更加鮮明。5 月消費者物價年增 3.2%，週末市場定價傾向 ECB 在 6 月 11 日升息，且年底前還會進一步緊縮。然而，1 年後起算、期間 1 年的通膨交換利率，已由 4 月高點 2.40% 降至 2.12%，第一季 GDP 修正值也顯示經濟萎縮。部分大型資產管理機構預期最多只升息一次。對中期債券而言，若升息僅是為了穩定通膨預期，疲弱成長仍可能支撐債價；若演變為持續緊縮，空間就小得多。

奧地利則出現個別財政風險。週五美國截止時間後，Morningstar DBRS 以赤字持續及債務趨勢逐步惡化為由，將評等由 AAA 降至 AA (high)。政府目標是在 2028 年前將赤字降至 GDP 的 3% 以下，但高能源與勞動成本仍拖累成長。奧地利 10 年期公債相對德債利差為 24 個基點，降評後市場即時反應有限。

## 主權償債、通膨與匯率壓力各有差異

塞內加爾在與 IMF 協商前，提前支付兩筆原定下週到期的票息：2037 年歐元債 €5,375 萬、2031 年美元債 $3,880 萬。短期付款風險因此降低，但國內償債日程仍緊迫，未來兩個月約需支付 7,380 億 CFA 法郎，全年計畫借款約 4 兆 CFA 法郎。IMF 因未揭露借款取消 $18 億融資安排後，當地發債天期縮短、成本提高，流動性更為吃緊。

哥倫比亞週五稍晚公布的通膨，增加恢復升息的理由。年增率由 5.68% 升至 5.84%，月增 0.47%，一項核心指標達 5.79%，整體數字接近市場預測中位數 5.9%。央行 4 月在董事會承受政治壓力之際，意外維持利率 11.25% 不變，如今通膨再度向上，使續抱長天期債券面臨更大的政策風險。

伊朗戰爭爆發以來，南韓、巴西、南非與墨西哥殖利率已上升逾 40 個基點。通膨預期解釋了大部分升幅，但政府補貼燃料與食品增加財政負擔，實質殖利率也隨之走高。即使和平協議使油價下降，前端可能先受惠，長端仍需消化國防支出、能源投資、AI 資本需求及較弱的財政狀況。

巴西指標殖利率維持在 14% 以上，政府總債務超過 GDP 的 80%，經濟成長仍強。南韓 10 年期殖利率接近兩年高點 4.25%，追加預算帶來的發債，疊加通膨與半導體需求所形成的壓力。

印尼週末的干預，則是處理更迫切的匯率與融資壓力。印尼盾年內已貶約 8%，跌破每美元 18,000，外資自債市淨撤出 $4.22 億。官方支撐限制了 10 年期公債跌幅，並承諾提供更多流動性。印尼央行另提議提高政府存放央行款項的利息，以抵銷部分上升的國家借款成本。方案的規模與條件仍待釐清：能源補貼已增加預算壓力，這類安排也可能使財政與貨幣政策的界線更加模糊。

中國加強境外投資課稅，可能影響民間資金流向。稅務機關向富裕居民追徵投資收益最高 20% 的稅款，並可能加計逾期罰款；中信證券估計，最多 HK$2,500 億香港資產可能受影響。此前一年，居民資金外流估計創下 $8,070 億紀錄。加強執法可能促使資產匯回、留住境內資金，同時降低境外投資的風險承擔意願。

官方準備則呈現中國對外部波動的另一層緩衝。5 月底外匯準備增加 $317 億，月增 0.93%，達 $3.4422 兆。外匯管理機關表示，變動主要來自匯率換算與全球資產價格。龐大的準備存量仍有助應對波動，但單月增加並不能證明有新的資金流入或干預。

## 接下來看通膨與標售

6 月 10 日美東時間 08:30 公布的美國 CPI，是檢驗非農後賣壓的下一個重點。市場預估 5 月整體 CPI 月增 0.5%、年增 4.2%，前值分別為 0.6% 與 3.8%；核心月增率預期由 0.4% 降至 0.3%。PPI 與初領失業金將在 6 月 11 日 08:30 公布，整體與核心 PPI 月增率預估為 0.6% 與 0.5%。若基礎物價壓力放緩，且初領人數高於前次 22.5 萬人，投資人就有理由重新評估目前完全反映的年底前升息；若物價普遍偏強，Fed 對就業反彈置之不理的空間將更小。

全週供給也相當密集：6 月 8 日標售 $890 億 13 週券與 $770 億 26 週券，6 月 9 日接續 $650 億 6 週券與 $500 億 52 週券；6 月 9–11 日附息債標售包括 $580 億 3 年期新券，以及 $390 億 10 年期、$220 億 30 年期增額發行。得標利率相對當時市場的水準、投標倍數、配售結構與交易商承接比重，將呈現需求能否跟上。買回操作可改善符合資格券種的流動性，但新增存續期間仍需由市場吸收，交割前後的國庫券利率則有助觀察現金壓力。

海外日程包括 6 月 10 日中國 5 月通膨與加拿大央行決策、6 月 11 日 ECB 決策，以及 6 月 12 日印度 CPI。市場預估中國消費者與生產者物價分別年增 1.4% 與 3.5%，印度通膨為 4.00%，加拿大維持利率 2.25%，ECB 升息 25 個基點。在強勁就業與歐洲疲弱產出並存之下，後續是否繼續升息的指引，會與當次決策同樣重要。

數據之外，週末也留下政策與地緣風險。Fed 理事 Michael Barr 警告，放寬銀行資本、流動性與監理，可能使脆弱性累積並最終損及放款，與 Michelle Bowman 主導的鬆綁方向形成分歧。澤倫斯基提出全面停火與直接和平談判，普丁卻在英、法、德領袖準備與澤倫斯基會面前拒絕會談，烏克蘭衝突短期降溫的空間仍有限。另一方面，美國與伊朗的談判仍是油價及通膨展望的關鍵。

美國 5 月非農就業增加 17.2 萬人，前兩個月上修，失業率維持 4.3%，使交換市場完全反映 Fed 在 12 月前升息 25 個基點。2 年期美債殖利率上升 12 個基點至 4.17%，10 年期上升 8 個基點至 4.55%；10 年期升幅全數來自實質殖利率，損益兩平通膨率維持 2.36%。

加拿大就業回升、日本薪資增強與印度上修通膨預測，都加重全球政策壓力；加拿大薪資放緩、歐元區經濟萎縮，則使後續路徑更不一致。6 月 10–11 日美國通膨與全週美債標售，將檢驗這波賣壓；週末的主權、監理與地緣消息，也為下一次開盤留下風險。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Payrolls Put a Fed Hike Back in the Price

A stronger-than-expected US jobs report sent Treasury yields sharply higher on Friday, wiping out Thursday's modest rally and leaving investors pricing a Federal Reserve increase by December. May payrolls rose 172,000, exceeding every forecast, and the previous two months were revised upward. The 2-year yield jumped 12 basis points to 4.17%, while the 10-year rose 8 to 4.55%.

The selloff came despite another decline in oil. The entire increase in the 10-year nominal yield was matched by its real yield, which reached 2.19%, while breakeven inflation held at 2.36%. Strong hiring had changed the outlook for policy and the return investors demanded after inflation. It also exposed an already vulnerable technology rally: the semiconductor index plunged 10.26%, the dollar strengthened and gold fell.

Borrowers nevertheless continued to secure financing. A Google-linked municipal issue traded at tighter spreads after its sale, and Apollo and Blackstone finalized $35 billion of debt for chips to be leased by Anthropic. Their terms showed substantial differences in the price of guaranteed and unguaranteed risk. Outside the US, strong Canadian hiring, firmer Japanese wages and a higher Indian inflation forecast reinforced the pressure on central banks to stay restrictive. The coming inflation releases will determine how much of Friday's more hawkish pricing survives.

## Hiring Sends the Front End Higher

The May employment report reversed the impression of cooling left by Thursday's claims data. Unemployment held at 4.3%, participation stayed at 61.8%, and leisure and hospitality added 70,000 jobs, its largest contribution in more than three years. Treasuries fell immediately after the release; the 2-year yield's intraday increase was its biggest in more than a year.

Interest-rate swaps fully priced a quarter-point Fed increase by December and put the probability of an October move at roughly 60%. June was still expected to bring a hold. Ahead of the new chairman's first meeting, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said an increase might soon be appropriate with employment near balance. Economists remained divided: Citi retained its forecast for three quarter-point cuts late in the year as hiring softened, while Goldman Sachs dropped its December cut call but still considered an increase unlikely.

The repricing was concentrated in the front half of the Treasury curve. The 5-year yield rose 11 basis points to 4.29% and the 30-year added 4 to 5.01%. The 2s10s spread narrowed 4 basis points to 38, and 2s30s narrowed 8 to 84. For the week, yields were up 19 basis points at two years, 16 at five, 10 at ten and only 2 at thirty. The 2s5s10s butterfly increased 2 basis points to −14, leaving the 5-year relatively rich to its wings; 2s10s30s was unchanged at −8.

Real yields followed the same pattern. The 5-year rose 11 basis points to 1.81%, the 7-year added 9 to 1.99%, and the 10-year increased 8 to 2.19%. The 20- and 30-year real yields rose 5 and 3 basis points to 2.55% and 2.74%. With the 10-year breakeven unchanged on the day and lower over the preceding week and month, the selloff was driven by higher real rates rather than another rise in long-term inflation compensation.

Later data showed households continuing to borrow. Consumer credit increased $20.73 billion in April, above the $17.80 billion consensus, after a revised $22.23 billion gain in March. Credit expanded at a 4.8% annual rate, led by revolving balances at 10.4%; nonrevolving credit rose 2.9%. The 15:00 ET release followed the morning's repricing. Faster card borrowing could reflect either sustained spending or financial strain, leaving the condition of household finances less clear than the payroll headline.

The shortest bills barely moved. Coupon-equivalent yields on 4-, 6- and 8-week bills held at 3.68%, 3.68% and 3.69%, and the 13-week remained at 3.71%. Yields rose 2, 3 and 5 basis points at 17, 26 and 52 weeks, respectively, as the expected policy increase affected later maturities. Options buyers also sought July 10-year calls targeting a yield decline toward 4.4% across the inflation releases and Fed meeting, a hedge against softer data or less hawkish guidance.

## Technology Losses Deepen as Financing Continues

Technology shares bore the heaviest losses as higher real yields collided with a rapid prior rally. The Nasdaq 100 fell 4.77% and the semiconductor index lost 10.26%, against a 2.64% decline in the S&P 500. VIX jumped 39.68% to 21.51. Profit-taking, a disappointing Broadcom outlook, possible Meta equity financing, bitcoin weakness and cash raising ahead of large offerings compounded the rate shock. Five S&P 500 sectors still advanced as investors shifted toward defensive industries.

The dollar index rose 0.66% to 100.07, and gold futures dropped 3.10% to $4,337.10. Oil moved in the opposite direction to the rates pressure: WTI fell 2.69% to $90.54 and Brent lost 2.04% to $93.09, although both remained higher for the week. Credit funds also fell, with LQD down 0.62%, HYG 0.50%, JNK 0.44% and EMB 0.73%.

In the primary market, financing tied to major technology companies continued to find buyers. The roughly $1 billion prepaid-energy issue sold by California Community Choice Financing Authority for Pioneer Community Energy used Alphabet as financial intermediary and Goldman Sachs as underwriter. Its largest portion priced 95 basis points over the benchmark. By Friday afternoon, $492 million of the 2035 bonds had traded at an average spread of 89 basis points, with some trades as tight as 74. The utility secured long-term electricity savings, while the new counterparty drew demand into the prepaid-energy market.

Apollo and Blackstone's completed $35 billion chip financing was much larger and split investors' exposure into distinct layers. Anthropic will lease Google-designed chips through a special-purpose vehicle, and about half the debt was syndicated. A $6 billion senior tranche priced 1 percentage point over Treasuries; another $24 billion of senior notes priced at par with a 5.75% coupon. Both carried private mid-investment-grade ratings and Broadcom support.

The $4.5 billion B tranche, without Broadcom backing, priced at par with an 8.5% coupon. If a defaulted lease forces a chip sale that fails to repay senior investors, Broadcom has agreed to cover the shortfall. That protection helped bring insurers and banks into the senior debt, while the junior tranche retained greater exposure to lease payments and chip resale values.

The scale of borrowing remains a concern even as individual deals clear. Weekend commentary from DoubleLine and Oaktree emphasized technology obsolescence, simultaneous data-center construction and uncertainty over eventual winners. Hyperscalers had sold more than $155 billion of unsecured bonds globally, already over 45% above the entire prior year's issuance. Bloomberg Intelligence estimated AI capital expenditure of roughly $5 trillion over five years, much of it financed with debt. The managers favored durable balance sheets and stronger recovery prospects without arguing that current bond valuations already constituted a bubble.

After the US close, President Donald Trump said a Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac share sale remained under consideration but was not urgent. Earlier proposals envisaged selling 5%–15% at a valuation of about $500 billion or more, potentially raising around $30 billion. The shares had fallen more than 30% during the year as doubts about execution grew. Capitalization, government support and the terms of any exit from conservatorship remain important for agency funding and mortgage rates; some analysts warned a sale could increase borrowing costs.

Elsewhere, new financing involved more difficult balance-sheet adjustments. Raizen disclosed after the close an out-of-court agreement covering about 65 billion reais, or $12.6 billion, of debt. Creditors holding 75.5% of the obligations supported the plan, which would convert 45% into equity and exchange 55% for new debt. In Japan, weekend figures showed debt at reporting Nikkei 225 companies reaching ¥678 trillion in the fiscal year through March, up 4.6%, as acquisitions, investment and shareholder distributions consumed cash. Nippon Steel's borrowing doubled around its $14 billion purchase of United States Steel, contributing to an S&P downgrade. Higher domestic rates will add to refinancing costs, particularly for weaker industrial borrowers; lending that grows faster than deposits may also push more funding into bond markets.

## Stronger Jobs and Wages Complicate Global Policy

Canada supplied another upside hiring surprise. Employment rose 87,800 in May, the most since December 2024, against a forecast of 10,000, and unemployment fell to 6.6% from 6.9%. Full-time hiring and gains across industries sent the 2-year yield about 10 basis points higher to 2.911%, its biggest intraday rise since May 4. Swaps priced more than 30 basis points of tightening by December.

The rebound did not erase the earlier weakness. Employment remained almost 25,000 below the end of 2025, while permanent full-time wage growth slowed to 3.2% from 4.8%, below the 4.6% forecast. The Bank of Canada is expected to hold at 2.25%; its guidance must now weigh a substantial hiring recovery against slower pay growth and the preceding job losses.

Japanese wage data strengthened expectations for a quarter-point BOJ increase at the June 15–16 meeting. Real pay rose 1.9% from a year earlier, beating the 1.7% forecast and revised 1.4% prior gain, for a fourth consecutive increase. Nominal wages climbed 3.5%, base pay 3.4%, and the full-time-worker measure watched by the BOJ 2.6%. The durability of those gains still depends on corporate profits and inflation as Middle East risks persist.

India's central bank unanimously held the repo rate at 5.25% and retained its neutral stance, but raised its fiscal-year inflation forecast to 5.1% from 4.6%. The standing deposit facility stayed at 5.00%, and the marginal standing facility and Bank Rate at 5.50%. The higher price forecast leaves less scope for an early easing despite the unchanged policy rate.

Taiwan's data also showed rising imported cost pressure. May consumer inflation accelerated to 2.20% from 1.74% year on year despite a smaller monthly increase. Producer prices rose 14.11%, up from 8.54%, while US-dollar import prices increased 17.21%. Softer monthly producer prices had not yet removed the pressure from imported inputs and currency translation.

Europe faced a sharper conflict between inflation and growth. May consumer inflation reached 3.2%, and weekend market pricing favored an ECB increase on June 11 with substantial further tightening by year-end. Yet the 1-year, 1-year inflation swap had fallen to 2.12% from April's 2.40% peak, and revised first-quarter data showed output contracting. Some large asset managers expected at most one increase. The distinction matters for intermediate bonds: a limited move to contain inflation expectations leaves more room for weak growth to support prices than a sustained tightening cycle would.

Austria added an issuer-specific fiscal concern. After Friday's US cutoff, Morningstar DBRS cut its rating to AA (high) from AAA, citing persistent deficits and a gradually worsening debt trajectory. The government aims to reduce the deficit below 3% of GDP by 2028, while high energy and labor costs weigh on growth. Austrian 10-year bonds yielded 24 basis points over Germany, with a limited immediate reaction to the downgrade.

## Sovereign Payments, Inflation and Currency Pressure

Senegal made two bond payments early ahead of IMF talks: €53.75 million on its 2037 euro bond and $38.8 million on its 2031 dollar notes, both due the following week. That eased the immediate payment risk but left a demanding domestic schedule. About 738 billion CFA francs of debt service falls due over two months, against planned annual borrowing of roughly 4 trillion CFA francs. Shorter, more expensive local issuance is tightening liquidity after the IMF canceled a $1.8 billion facility over undisclosed borrowing.

Colombia's later Friday inflation release increased the case for renewed tightening. Annual inflation rose to 5.84% from 5.68%, with prices up 0.47% on the month and a core measure at 5.79%. The headline was close to the 5.9% median forecast. Its upward direction is nevertheless uncomfortable for a central bank that unexpectedly held at 11.25% in April amid political pressure on the board.

Across South Korea, Brazil, South Africa and Mexico, yields had risen more than 40 basis points since the Iran war began. Inflation expectations accounted for much of the increase, but higher real yields also reflected fiscal costs from fuel and food support. Lower oil following a peace agreement could help front ends before it relieved longer maturities, where defense spending, energy investment, AI capital needs and weaker budgets would remain.

Brazilian benchmark yields stayed above 14%, with gross public debt exceeding 80% of GDP and growth still firm. Korea's 10-year yield was near a two-year high at 4.25%, as supplementary-budget issuance added to pressure from inflation and semiconductor-led demand.

Indonesia's weekend intervention addressed a more immediate currency and funding strain. The rupiah had lost about 8% during the year and passed 18,000 per dollar, while foreigners had withdrawn a net $422 million from bonds. Official support limited losses in 10-year debt, and authorities pledged additional liquidity. Bank Indonesia also proposed paying more interest on government deposits at the central bank to offset part of the state's higher borrowing cost. The scale and terms remain important: energy subsidies are already straining the budget, and the arrangement risks further blurring fiscal and monetary responsibilities.

China's effort to tax offshore investment could alter private capital flows. Authorities were pursuing wealthy residents for levies of as much as 20% on investment gains, plus possible late-payment penalties. Citic Securities estimated that up to HK$250 billion of Hong Kong assets could be affected, following estimated record resident outflows of $807 billion in the prior year. Enforcement may encourage repatriation and retain domestic capital, while reducing offshore risk appetite.

Official reserves offered a different view of China's external position. End-May foreign-exchange reserves rose $31.7 billion, or 0.93%, to $3.4422 trillion. The foreign-exchange authority attributed the increase mainly to currency conversion and global asset-price changes. The large stock remains a buffer against volatility, though the monthly gain does not establish new capital inflows or intervention.

## Inflation and Auctions Come Next

US CPI at 08:30 ET on June 10 is the next major test of the payroll-driven selloff. Consensus expects May headline inflation of 0.5% on the month and 4.2% on the year, after 0.6% and 3.8%, with monthly core inflation slowing to 0.3% from 0.4%. PPI and initial claims follow at 08:30 ET on June 11; forecasts put headline and core PPI increases at 0.6% and 0.5%. Softer underlying prices, especially alongside claims rising from 225,000, would give investors reason to reconsider the fully priced year-end increase. Broad price strength would make it harder for the Fed to look through the hiring rebound.

Supply is substantial across the week: $89 billion of 13-week and $77 billion of 26-week bills on June 8, followed by $65 billion at six weeks and $50 billion at 52 weeks on June 9. Coupon auctions over June 9–11 comprise $58 billion of 3-year notes and reopenings of $39 billion at ten years and $22 billion at thirty. Clearing levels against prevailing trading, bid-to-cover ratios, bidder allocations and dealer retention will show whether demand keeps pace. Buybacks can support liquidity in eligible securities, but investors still need to absorb the new duration; bill rates around settlement will help identify any cash pressure.

The overseas calendar includes China's May inflation and the Bank of Canada decision on June 10, the ECB on June 11 and Indian CPI on June 12. Forecasts put Chinese consumer and producer inflation at 1.4% and 3.5% year on year, Indian inflation at 4.00%, a Canadian hold at 2.25% and an ECB increase of a quarter point. Guidance on further increases will matter as much as the decisions, given the contrast between strong labor data and Europe's weaker output.

Weekend developments also leave risks beyond the data calendar. Fed Governor Michael Barr warned that weaker bank capital, liquidity and supervision could allow vulnerabilities to build and eventually impair lending, challenging the deregulatory direction under Michelle Bowman. Volodymyr Zelenskyy offered a full ceasefire and direct peace talks, but Vladimir Putin rejected a meeting ahead of planned talks between Zelenskyy and UK, French and German leaders. That leaves little immediate relief from the Ukraine conflict, while the separate US-Iran negotiations remain central to oil and the inflation outlook.
